verdict.rationale: Discord documents an official REST API that authenticates with either a bot token or an OAuth2 bearer token, and its OAuth2 docs describe scope-like permissions. Sending messages into channels is documented, though via webhooks, which need no authentication, and the Gateway delivers server events. The pack never explicitly documents bot endpoints for reading or posting channel messages, or how token scopes limit those message operations. Missing for 10: explicit message read/create endpoint documentation, documented scope/permission granularity for channel messaging, hands-on or independent corroboration of an agent workflow.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent read and post channel messages through the official API using scoped tokens

citations.quote: The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.
Using a bot token found on the Bot page within your app’s settings... Using an OAuth2 bearer token gained through the OAuth2 API.
Send messages into Discord channels or receive event notifications from Discord delivered to your app over HTTP.
allows /users/@me/connections to return linked third-party accounts
